metadata.title: Nonmonotone Argument and Radial Angle of a Support Slit
metadata.description:
Every global maximizer of the real part of a2+i*10^-24(a4-3a3) in the normalized schlicht class omits a slit with nonmonotone continuous argument and nonmonotone signed and ordinary unsigned radial angles. This gives negative answers to the two questions recorded as Hayman-Lingham Problem 6.72. Compactness provides genuine extremizers, the area theorem bounds the actual slit tip, and a controlled Schiffer natural coordinate identifies a subarc of the actual omitted slit. No explicit maximizing function or uniqueness is required.

The 5-page research note credits the classical support-slit geometry, Schiffer methods and Friedland-Schiffer coefficient/control framework and is accompanied by manuscript source, immutable authored input, independent analytic and quantitative derivations, exact rational and directed interval checks and a bounded primary-source priority audit. Complete Zemyan2003/2005/2007, Duren1983, Zhang–Ma1991, Brickman1984 and Goh1994 comparisons are recorded; the 2014 Duren commentary and Goh1992 coefficient article remain material uninspected comparisons; no historical-first priority or continued open status in 2026 is asserted. Finite controls supplement the uniform analytic proofs and are not formal certification of the classical inputs.

AI tools were used extensively in development, writing, reproduction and adversarial verification. This is an unrefereed preprint with internal AI adversarial reviews; it has not received human peer review.
